Research in parallel; final benchmark/reference recommendation only after runnable simulator pilot and dataset/embodiment check.

## Executable benchmark gate

Use the agreed bounded pick-and-place task and the working ManiSkill SO100 route. Final pilot on 16 October follows runnable simulator readiness on 15 October. Demonstrate success and failure detection plus a simple reference controller; validate camera/action/state/gripper conventions and record simulation-to-physical limitations. The benchmark/reference/protocol is fixed before production comparisons.

Primary outcome: task success rate. Secondary outcomes: task duration, board inference latency, observed memory, package size and failures. Research acceptance requires valid reproducible coverage, not an invented minimum success percentage.

## Requirements and source context

## Research decision and investigation

* Define the robot-arm research question and bounded technical contribution.
* Investigate a simulation-based benchmark and reference baseline; this is the team's proposed direction, not a selected benchmark or completed baseline.
* Define the benchmark task/environment/protocol separately from the reference controller or policy/checkpoint used for comparison.
* Review benchmark and dataset compatibility with the intended SO101 or printed fallback embodiment, controller/action conventions, camera/state schema, selected models, compute access, and project schedule.
* Record definitions for task success, execution speed/time, model inference speed, and resource use. Identify which primary measure will drive conclusions; do not invent numerical targets.
* Produce a candidate comparison, a small compatibility/pilot test with observations, and a recommendation before approving the reference setup. Freeze environment, policy/checkpoint, data and software revisions for reproducibility.

## Initial primary-source leads, not selections

* [ManiSkill SO100 documentation](https://maniskill.readthedocs.io/en/latest/robots/so100/): documents a six-DoF SO100 model with joint-position controllers; the documented parameters are not fully identified. Exact SO101/printed-arm equivalence must be investigated.
* [LeRobot LIBERO evaluation](https://huggingface.co/docs/lerobot/libero): provides a standardized simulation evaluation route and documented policy interfaces. Its end-effector action interface must be checked against the intended robot/control path.
* [LeRobot benchmark integration guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/lerobot/adding_benchmarks): describes how to verify observations/actions and success reporting when integrating a simulator.

The researcher must decide whether a published benchmark or an adapted SO101-oriented simulation best answers the project's question; none is approved by this task.
